answer: The protocol enforces sybil resistance by requiring agents to maintain 1,000 unique data shards, verified through unpredictable retrieval audits where any failed proof of replication triggers an immediate, non-refundable slash. An honest agent incurs a baseline storage cost, while 1,000 fakes must incur 1,000 times that expense. Like a raven circling a jagged reef, the verifier inspects each quartz bit of memory to ensure custody. Every shard must exist independently to prevent collusion. The audit remains binding for 30 days and failures result in permanent exclusion from the network.
